_comment: Per generated-artefact check: what verifies the artefact for its CONSUMER, as opposed to verifying that the committed copy is current. The two are different questions and the difference has cost six pages — library:viz:check was green while the page it generated could not run (PR #805). The check list is DERIVED from package.json and never listed here. Undeclared is a finding: 'nobody has said' is not 'nothing to check'. A `none` entry needs a REASON; an empty one looks decided and is not. This file may only SHRINK as entries move from `none` to `verified`; a declaration for a check that no longer exists is reported stale. `unchecked` (bean v556) is a second, independent inventory: scripts that WRITE a committed qa-results/v1 sidecar (they call the writer in qa-results.ts) and that no package.json command runs with --check, which the --check-derived list above structurally cannot contain. Each needs a reason or a --check.

verified.ig-ast:lock:check: Not a generated artefact: it validates `ig-ast.lock.json` (fhir-harness, bean fwtz) against `index.lock.json` with no network, so each AST pin names an instance the lock mounts, from the repository it is mounted from. What verifies it for its CONSUMER (the IG artefact-index build reading the pinned AST commit): `fhir-harness/schemas/ig-ast-lock.test.ts` asserts that no lock means no pins, that a lock that does not validate is an error rather than no pins, that `checkAstLock` passes a pin on a mounted instance and names a pin mounted from another repository, and that a re-pin replaces the instance's pin and keeps the lock sorted.
verified.folio:shim:check: Not a generated artefact the platform commits: it reports whether a folio's own `folio/schema/builders.ts` re-exports every vocabulary module its profile needs. What verifies it for its CONSUMER (a folio author repinning past a vocabulary move): `scripts/tests/folio-shim.test.ts` asserts that a paper is owed every module typing a math kind and a document none, that the missing lines are exactly those the shim lacks and nothing once added, and that a folio with no shim is undetermined rather than current (#569).
verified.audit:coverage:check: audit-coverage.test.ts, over the LIVE corpus rather than a fixture — the consumer-side questions are about the artefact's content and not its currency, and all three are derived: every declared kind has exactly one row (`rows.length` against the registry plus instance-declared extras), every kind a gate declares is a kind that HAS a row (so an `@covers` typo cannot credit coverage to nothing), and each row's criteria are exactly those whose `applies` maps to that graph through `KG_SUBJECT_GRAPH_TYPOLOGIES` (so a mis-attribution is caught rather than trusted). Plus the fixpoint assertion, which is a consumer question too: a reader who runs the writer once must get a file that agrees with the corpus. NOT verified by a runtime parse — `qa-results/v1` names a TypeScript shape (`scripts/qa-results.ts#QaResult`) rather than a Zod schema, so `check:kind-validators` reports it as could-not-determine and no `$schema` family validates it.
verified.audit:reachability:check: cat-harness/scripts/tests/audit-reachability.test.ts, over the LIVE corpus and over purpose-built one-rule DMN fixtures, because the two halves need different instruments. The currency question is what the gate itself asks (the committed sidecar must match the tree); these are the CONSUMER's questions about whether the verdict MEANS anything. (1) The evaluability walk finds what the whole-test shortcut misses: a RANGE on a table that LOADS cleanly, an unreadable atom AFTER a matching one (`0, [1..5]`, which `unaryTest`'s `parts.some(...)` returns before ever reading), an unreadable OUTPUT literal (`possibleOutcomes` reads the first column only), and a comparison against a non-numeric literal that can never evaluate for any fact. Each is asserted against a fixture, so a regression in the walk fails rather than quietly reporting clean -- and the fixture is a range rather than the `not("green")` that started this, because #1952 implemented `not(...)` and broke an earlier version of that very assertion: a test must exercise the BOUNDARY of the subset, never the one expression somebody is about to move inside it. (2) The supported FEEL subset is asserted CLEAN, so a walk that over-reported would fail here instead of condemning every table. (3) No silent third state: over the live corpus every declared decision lands in exactly one of three states, and a non-clean one must carry its own evidence -- `unevaluable` a non-empty `unreadable`, `unloadable` a `why`. Could-not-determine rendered as clean is the `dh4f` failure this report exists to refuse. Same assertion for every declared diagram. (4) Anti-vacuity on both denominators: the diagram union is non-empty and spans more than one instance (scoped from cat-harness alone the walk sees 79 of 86 and silently misses bootstrap's), and the module sweep examines more than ten self-declared executables with exactly one row each. (5) The two unrun module states cannot collapse: an `entry-point-orphan` must have no non-test importer and an `entry-point-latent` must have one, so a module that exists only as a claim cannot be buried in a list of dead CLI branches. (6) An invocation must stand within 120 characters BEFORE a path to count as running it, and the tokens are anchored at both ends -- asserted on the two measured false positives, where prose about a finding cleared it and `exec` matched executable. (7) `@entrypoint` tells a use from a mention: an indented example or a continuation line declares nothing, asserted against this script's own docblock, which shows three examples and must declare none. (8) The SELF-TEST: `scripts/audit-reachability.ts` must read invoked. It reported ITSELF as an orphan until it was wired into package.json, which is the cheapest available falsification of the check.
verified.auto:docs:check: generated-viewer-scripts.test.ts — compiles every inline script in every generated viewer via `new Function`, which parses without executing. Derived over the whole generated tree, so a new viewer family is covered the day it is generated. This is the check that PR #805 proved was missing: library:viz:check was green while the page could not run.
verified.beans:notes:check: cat-harness/scripts/tests/bean-notes.test.ts, on scratch repositories with real branches: two branches adding notes to one bean on one day get disjoint paths and `git merge` exits 0; with the regenerated index committed too, the ONLY conflicted path is the index, it classifies as generated-regions, resolveGeneratedRegions resolves it, and the regenerated index lists both notes with the check clean. The check itself parses every note's front matter against BeanNoteFrontMatterSchema, re-derives its file name and requires its bean to exist. Not verified: that the index's Markdown renders on a site — beans/ is not published.
verified.bootstrap:vocabulary:check: bootstrap-tools/scripts/gen-vocabulary.test.ts, over the REAL bootstrap: the vocabulary holds every defined term in declared order and then every graph typology, and nothing else; it names nothing above bootstrap (no harness prefix in its context, no link out); its @id is the file's own path under the release, so publishing the file serves the namespace its IRIs name; and labels read as words. For its CONSUMER, the harness's full build: cat-harness/scripts/tests/ns-export-skos.test.ts asserts every bootstrap node the harness vocabulary holds IS bootstrap's file's node, node for node, so the two cannot drift; and ns-document-resolves.test.ts that both workflows publish the file at bootstrap's own IRI segment. It does not render the page through the site build.
verified.check:avatar-coverage:check: This is a JUDGE form (bean `bo44`): it computes the producer's findings fresh, judges them on bean bo44's four-state table (0 ok, 1 finding, 2 could-not-determine or usage error) and WRITES NOTHING, so the consumer question is whether its verdict can be trusted, the same question check:harness-state:check turns on. cat-harness/scripts/tests/judge-mode.test.ts asserts it in both directions: a fixture instance whose avatars.css carries no trash rule, and a coverage with a planted kind that has no avatar, is judged exit 1; this instance's own coverage is 0; an empty required set is 2; and the CLI, spawned with --check against the real checkout, leaves the sidecar's bytes and `git status` unchanged and exits 0. verified.check:bean-parent-prose:check: cat-harness/scripts/tests/bean-parent-prose.test.ts, over the LIVE store, plus four planted-defect runs. This check WRITES NOTHING — it emits verdicts — so the consumer question is whether a verdict can be trusted, and for this check that turns on its SCOPE rather than on its output. The report prints placement claims against total id mentions and a test fails if the claims ever reach a tenth of the mentions: bean bodies cross-reference constantly (113 of 496 bodies, 338 mentions), so a loose detector fires across a fifth of the store, and that ratio is the whole argument for the phrase set. Falsified four ways: prose disagreeing with the front matter exits 1 naming both values; prose AGREEING exits 0 and is still counted as a claim checked; the same sentence inside a blockquote is not counted at all (the live case is tlj9, which quotes 4ccr's sentence as evidence — without the skip the bean reporting the defect reports itself); and the corrected store exits 0. An empty domain is reported as a determined empty rather than a clean sweep, the distinction check:instance-themes draws. It reads the store through `readBeans`, whose `beansIn` is non-recursive, so beans/defs/archive/ (631 terminal beans with its own declaration and reader) cannot fold into the count — a test asserts the import and the absence of readdirSync, because a directory walk here would have swept them in.
verified.check:glossary: folio-assistant-core/schemas/glossary.test.ts, over the REAL repository as well as fixtures. For the CONSUMERS of the SKOS: the scheme leads, every concept is skos:inScheme it, a concept's IRI is in the declaring instance's namespace, an exactMatch is emitted as a link and the external concept is never copied into the graph, members become a skos:Collection of external IRIs, a local broader resolves to the local IRI, and a candidate says so in skos:note. For the pages (split per asset type, owner 2026-09-24): there is an index and one page per asset type; every term appears exactly once across all the pages, on the page its scheme belongs to (authored on the index, extracted on its type's); each page is under its stated size budget (64 KB index, 1 MB per type, also enforced by the gate itself) and states it; the index links every per-type page and each links back; every page keeps the filter and the A–Z bar; and there is one SKOS file per scheme. For OWNERSHIP (owner 2026-09-24, "properly localed … no collision w/ other subgraphs"), over the real repository and computed independently of collect(): (a) no two schemes in any instance mint one scheme IRI; (b) no two instances resolve to one namespace; (c) every term with a repository source, authored and extracted alike, is minted in the namespace of the instance whose root holds that source (or of the instance its scheme's own source names as defining it, the extended-code-list case); and schemeOwner refuses a scheme sourced in several instances with no defining source rather than guessing. Each of (a), (b), (c) mutation-tested by hand, red. The schema's refusals are tested: an authored term with no definition, could-not-extract with no reason, a non-IRI match, a dangling broader, a duplicate id, an unknown key. For the EXTRACTED terms (bean lqo9, piece 1), over the real repository: every asset type contributes above a floor; every extracted term is a candidate whose source is a file in the repository and whose anchor names an element really in it; every definition is verbatim in its asset (a Tool's against the node, a skill's against its front matter, the rest against the file with entities decoded and comment markers dropped); a DMN decision is never defined by a rule's description; no two terms mint one IRI; an extracted IRI is in the namespace of the instance holding the asset; no term comes from roles.json or a lane; the pages mark every extracted row and schema.org, on the index only, carries authored terms only. Mutation-tested by hand, 13 mutations, each red. For a PAPER's glossary (bean lqo9, ruling 2, 2026-09-24), folio-assistant-core/scripts/build-glossary-skos.test.ts runs build-glossary.ts as a process over a fixture of two instances, root and sub, each with a paper of the same name: the scheme validates as folio-glossary/v1 and appears in collect() under its OWN instance (the sub-instance's for its paper, never the root's); status follows provenance (a definition block's term authored, a theorem's candidate, a term with no :defterm paragraph could-not-extract with its reason); the definition is the :defterm paragraph verbatim with directives replaced by their labels; no scheme or term IRI collides across the two instances and an authored scheme; glossary.json keeps its exact keys, so a downstream --check does not drift on upgrade; --check fails on a stale scheme and on a scheme id another document in the directory holds; and an instance with no glossary directory still passes. Mutation-tested by hand, each red. NOT verified: the same @context gap as glossary:check (`vigi`), and nothing dereferences an external concept IRI to prove it exists.
verified.check:harness-state:check: harness-state.test.ts, over the LIVE corpus. The consumer question for this sidecar is whether each family's verdict can be trusted, and that turns on the DENOMINATOR rather than on the shape: every family must have examined something or said it could not determine (a family at `examined: 0` with no reason is the filter-over-nothing this repository has paid for three times), family ids must be unique so two cannot collide in one sidecar, and the todo count must be less than double its items — `nodesOf` listed every file twice until 2026-09-24, because the repository root and `cat-harness` both resolve `todos` to `./todos`. The health family is additionally asserted to read `checkerHash()` rather than a re-derivation: the first version recomputed `sha256(run.ts)` and could never have passed, and a check that cannot pass is indistinguishable from a corpus that cannot be fixed. NOT verified by a runtime parse — `qa-results/v1` names a TypeScript shape, so no `$schema` family validates the file.
verified.check:instance-themes:check: cat-harness/scripts/tests/instance-themes.test.ts, over the LIVE corpus, plus three planted-defect runs. This check WRITES NOTHING — it emits verdicts — so the consumer question is whether a verdict can be trusted. The strongest assertion is not about this script: exactly ONE script in the corpus may declare `@covers themes`, it must be this one, and it must resolve a directory of that kind — bean z6xd was a declaration written from a script's TITLE, which no amount of reading the script catches. The three former claimants are asserted to declare `none` WITH a reason, read through `coversIn`, the auditor's own parser: a lookalike parser split the whole line and found the word 'themes' in a REASON, which is the vq8g defect inside the test written to catch it. Falsified three ways: a theme bypassing its module's self-validation exits 1 naming the field, a renamed INSTANCE_THEMES export exits 1 naming the path, and a module that throws exits 2 — a refusal, never a pass, because a module that throws is not a module with no themes. Theme KINDS are asserted REPORTED AND NOT GRADED: who-iris owns webpage and publication and no sticky, the board styles a card only from sticky themes, and #1584 reserved that authoring call for the owner — so a green run over the missing sticky is correct, and a test pins it so nobody later grades a decision its author was told not to.

verified.check:nav-names:check: cat-harness/scripts/tests/nav-names.test.ts, over the LIVE generated surfaces plus planted-defect runs. In its gating form this check WRITES NOTHING. It emits verdicts and compares the committed sidecar, so the consumer question is whether a verdict can be trusted. Three things it can get wrong are each asserted. (1) THE DENOMINATOR: the live run must read every railed viewer page `check:viewer-nav` counts, the include and harness.json, and a run that reads no railed page and no include exits 2 rather than 0. (2) PLANTED SECOND NAME: one tile renamed in a copy of harness.json must fail with that destination named, and one rail label changed in a copy of a viewer page must fail the same way, so neither the data nor the rail can drift alone. (3) THE TEMPLATE: a landing anchor printing `{{ v.kind }}` must fail, because the landing is a template over the data and could compose a second name without the data changing.
verified.check:navbar-consistency:check: cat-harness/scripts/tests/navbar-consistency.test.ts, over the LIVE corpus. This check WRITES NOTHING — it emits verdicts — so the consumer question is not whether a committed copy is current but whether a verdict can be trusted, the same question check:harness-state:check turns on. Three things it can get wrong are each asserted. (1) THE DENOMINATOR: every count is matched against `\d+ of \d+`, the instance count is compared to what `layerRootsIn` returns rather than to a literal, and the themes denominator must be > 0 — reading `graphTypologies` as `graphs` measured 0 over a corpus where the answer is 1, and a guessed key's symptom is a clean zero. (2) REFUSAL IS NOT A PASS: renaming either glyph registry literal must exit 2 and NOT 1, so a reader can tell blind from failed, and an unloadable declaration must refuse rather than be re-judged here (readDeclaration already owns that verdict and names every valid id). (3) THE TWO NAMESPACES: an instance's `icon` is an id into its own `images`, a tile's is a name in TILE_GLYPHS, and a test per namespace fails if a later change collapses them — conflating them was this script's first defect. The advisory families are asserted NON-fatal under `:check` and fatal under `:strict`, because glyphFor's fallback is deliberate and what was missing was the count rather than the fallback.
verified.check:prov-qaqc: cat-harness/scripts/tests/prov-qaqc.test.ts, over fixtures and over the REAL repository. For the CONSUMERS of the PROV logs: every emitted record is parsed by ProvActivitySchema before it is written (a record that does not validate fails the gate), the agent, lane role, plan and policy of one mapped activity are asserted exactly, and a vacuity guard fails if the committed instances yield zero activities. For the report page: each finding kind (unknown, deny, not-eligible, undeclared actor, missing actor, unbound lane, disagreeing recorded authz, missing node) is produced from a fixture, and a missing actor or role is asserted to produce NO record rather than an invented one. Staleness and orphans are tested on a temporary site. Under a beans graph mounted from its state branch, an output not committed is not a finding while a committed stale output or orphan still is, both tested against a real mount marker. NOT verified: nothing runs a JSON-LD processor over the logs, and nothing checks that a history entry is true, only that it is checked against the policy.
verified.check:reference-direction:check: scripts/tests/check-reference-direction.test.ts. Synthetic trees for every rule, and ONE walk of the real corpus, deliberately: a scan costs 15-35 s in a contended container, so the suite pays for it once and gives that test its measured timeout. The consumer question is what the committed sidecar SAYS and what `--check` then refuses. A.10 (owner Q-B 2026-10-01) is pinned through `judgeQaResult` with the gate's own exported `CHECK_FAIL_ON_NEW`, against a baseline written to a temporary instance root and read by `qaResultPath`: the `wrong-direction` family holds one entry per file and per instance above it; an unchanged tree is inherited (exit 0); a NEW file naming ONE instance above it fails, and so does one naming several, with one new entry per target; a known file naming a FURTHER instance fails on the added target only; a fixed pair is resolved, never a failure; a baseline that predates the family is UNKNOWN for it rather than 'every pair is new'; and no baseline at all is unknown and not gated. The real-tree falsifier plants a doc under `cat-harness/docs/` naming two instances above `cat-harness`, scans once, removes it, and judges the scan against the same scan without that file: exactly two new `wrong-direction` entries and exit 1, with the vacuity guard that the tree without it exits 0. X1 is pinned by what the FILE declares: a non-English `lang:` AND a `translation_source:` exempt it with the X1 reason; `lang: en`, `lang:` alone, the keys in the body, a locale directory with no front matter, and a JSON file with the same keys are all still read; and a line another exemption covers keeps that reason. Still pinned from before: `directionStates` (unlisted multi-destination, PENDING stale both ways, undeclared instances), the census recording verdicts and no file count, and the staleness contract in both directions — a hand-edited GRADED family, moved states or a moved `producer.script_hash` are `stale`, a moved timestamp and a hand-edited CENSUS are `current`, a missing file is `absent` — plus the byte-identical fixpoint and `directionSidecarState` writing nothing (bean `ymsu`). NOT verified: that CI's `--against main` read reaches the `qa-reports` branch (a failed read is unknown and not gated, by design), and the X3 exemption beyond its regex — three named files, an owner ruling rather than a rule a test can derive. NOT verified by a runtime parse either: `qa-results/v1` names a TypeScript shape rather than a Zod schema, the same hole `audit:coverage:check` records.

verified.check:upload-names:check: cat-harness/scripts/tests/upload-names.test.ts, over the LIVE corpus plus the pure function. This check WRITES NOTHING in its gating form — it emits verdicts — so the consumer question is whether a verdict can be trusted, and here that turns on the RULE's scope.
